synthesis.summary: The panel converges sharply on a single architectural complaint: the patch inlines the entire compiled script into the compile_notebook RPC response and threads those bytes through 3-4 layers of React state when the file already exists on disk at a known path. Five of six reviewers (Knuth, Hickey, Torvalds, Pike, Dijkstra) want a download endpoint or fetch-by-path instead; Liskov frames it as a contract violation (the RPC's ADT silently changed from "return references" to "return references AND inline payload"). Secondary consensus: the unguarded open(script_path) has no encoding, no size bound, no error handling, and no stated invariant linking script_content to pipeline_package_path. The clickable GetAppIcon is flagged by all six as not-a-real-button (no keyboard activation, no role, no focus ring). The strongest preserved minor disagreement is on the dead-code fallback filename 'pipeline.kale.py': Knuth and Torvalds say drop or assert it; Dijkstra says the precondition on compiledPath was never stated at all (trailing slashes, Windows backslashes) so the fallback is symptom not cause. No reviewer dissents on severity of the main payload-shape issue — all rate it P1.

issues.description: Entire compiled script inlined into RPC response payload and React state with no size bound, when a path/handle already exists
issues.detail: The backend reads the full compiled .kale.py off disk and embeds it in every compile_notebook response, then the frontend carries it through Commands return, DeploysProgressState, props into DeployProgress, and finally into a Blob — three or four layers of state holding the same bytes for an action that may never happen. The file already exists at pipeline_package_path; the right shape is a download endpoint that streams from script_path on click, keeping the compile response O(1). Hickey calls this complecting reference and value; Liskov calls it a silent ADT contract change; Pike calls the data structure wrong; Torvalds calls it a fat payload for no reason; Dijkstra notes the redundant double-transport.

issues.description: open(script_path) is unguarded: no encoding declared, no size bound, no error handling, no stated precondition
issues.detail: The backend calls open(script_path) with the platform-default encoding, no try/except, and no upper bound on file size. A read failure (missing file, perm error, non-UTF8 bytes) now fails the entire compile_notebook RPC after compile_pipeline already succeeded — coupling a convenience download feature to the success path of the main operation. Dijkstra frames it as unstated precondition; Hickey wants explicit encoding='utf-8' and a size contract; Torvalds and Liskov want either a guard with fallback or a separation of the read into its own operation.

issues.description: No invariant tying compiledPath to compiledContent — two representations of the same artifact can desynchronize
issues.detail: The RPC returns both pipeline_package_path and script_content with no stated invariant that content == read(path). If anything rewrites script_path between compile_pipeline and the inline read, the 'Download' button will offer bytes that differ from what was actually compiled. Liskov names this as an abstraction leak and suggests a single CompiledArtifact value type at the boundary; Dijkstra frames it as an unenforced postcondition; Hickey wants the content carried once (ideally lazily fetched by path) rather than duplicated.

issues.description: Download icon (GetAppIcon) is rendered as a clickable SVG, not a real button — no keyboard, no role, no focus ring
issues.detail: The download trigger uses onClick directly on GetAppIcon with only titleAccess for an accessible name. It is not focusable, has no role='button', and cannot be activated by Enter/Space. The sibling 'Done' control uses a real <a>, so this also breaks consistency with surrounding code. Fix is small: wrap in IconButton, render as <button>, or use an <a download> with href={objectUrl}.

issues.description: handleDownloadClick reasons only about the happy path — no try/finally, leaks object URL on throw
issues.detail: The handler does Blob -> createObjectURL -> append anchor -> click -> remove -> revokeObjectURL imperatively with no try/finally. If click() or any prior step throws, revokeObjectURL never runs and the object URL leaks. Dijkstra labels this TESTED-NOT-PROVED. Liskov wants the DOM mechanics extracted into a downloadBlob(name, content) abstraction so revoke/append ordering is owned by one module. Pike and Hickey both prefer a declarative <a href={url} download={fileName}> rendered when content is available — no DOM mutation in an event handler at all.

issues.description: Filename fallback 'pipeline.kale.py' is dead code under the current guard and would mask bugs if reached
issues.detail: props.compiledPath.split('/').pop() || 'pipeline.kale.py' only fires the fallback if compiledPath is empty, but the outer branch already requires compiledPath to be truthy. Knuth and Torvalds call it dead code that would silently substitute a plausible-looking but wrong filename if ever reached. Liskov adds that this is the third inconsistent filename in the system (Commands.ts already owns 'kale.py' / 'pipeline.yaml'). Dijkstra goes further: the precondition on compiledPath was never stated, so trailing slashes and Windows backslashes are also unreasoned. Recommend: assert, drop the fallback, or pass the intended filename through state explicitly.

issues.description: Click handler silently no-ops when compiledContent is missing — user gets no feedback
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick guards on (compiledPath && compiledContent) and returns silently if either is absent. The icon is rendered based on compiledPath alone, so the user can see and click an affordance that does nothing. Hickey: identity (visible button) and value (bytes) are decoupled in a way the UI does not express. Liskov: the visible affordance and the operation's precondition are out of sync; either gate rendering on (compiledPath && compiledContent) or make compiledContent required in the success state. Dijkstra calls this a SMUGGLED-GOTO — control leaves the function with no signal.

issues.description: Blob/anchor download dance lacks a literate comment explaining the idiom
issues.detail: createObjectURL / detached anchor / click / revokeObjectURL is a well-known browser idiom but reads as five unrelated DOM operations. A 2-3 line comment stating the invariant ('synthesize a transient object URL, click a detached anchor to trigger the browser download UI, then release the URL') would make the function readable without running it.

issues.description: Blob MIME 'text/plain' for a .py file is inconsistent with content type
issues.detail: text/plain works for download but text/x-python is more accurate. Not a blocker today; would matter if this is ever wired to a preview surface.

issues.description: compiledContent typed as string only because failure mode is server-side crash
issues.detail: The TS type 'string' is technically honest only because a non-UTF8 byte will raise on the server before reaching the client, killing the whole compile RPC. The type's correctness depends on the unguarded backend read crashing earlier — making the type a downstream symptom of the upstream missing error handling.

dissents.topic: Whether the right fix is a separate download endpoint, a CompiledArtifact value type, or a declarative <a download> rendered from existing state

positions.position: Expose a small read-by-path endpoint (input: path, output: bytes); UI fetches on click. Classic Unix-filter shape, keeps compile response small and gets the bytes out of React state entirely.
Expose a download endpoint that streams from script_path. The file is already on disk; doubling every compile result's payload to avoid wiring a download endpoint is the wrong trade.
Switch to a handle (existing compiledPath) plus a GET /download?path=... endpoint — O(1) memory until the user clicks, vs. O(n) per compile today.

Either return the value with a content hash and drop the path coupling, OR keep the path and expose a separate explicit 'read compiled script' call. Don't complect a reference and a value in one response.
Commit explicitly to a single CompiledArtifact value type at the boundary, OR split content retrieval into a separate operation. The existing contract must be restated, not silently widened.
Reuse the existing link mechanism with a download attribute rather than introducing a parallel channel. State the invariant that link target and download target are the same bytes.

dissents.topic: Severity and framing of the dead 'pipeline.kale.py' fallback

positions.position: P2 dead code. Drop the fallback or assert; if it ever did fire it would lie about the filename.
P2 readability/safety. The fallback masks a real bug rather than exposes it; prefer asserting the invariant or logging.
P2 contract duplication. Commands.ts already owns the filename mapping; this is now a third inconsistent name. Pass intended filename through state explicitly.
P1-adjacent. The deeper issue is that the precondition on compiledPath was never stated at all — trailing slashes and Windows backslashes are unreasoned, the fallback is symptom not cause.

dissents.topic: How to handle the DOM-imperative download dance

positions.position: Keep the imperative idiom but add a literate comment explaining the blob/anchor sequence as a single invariant.
Replace with a declarative <a href={objectUrl} download={fileName}> memoized and revoked on unmount. The current code is easy (familiar idiom) but not simple.
Replace with a plain <a href={url} download={fileName}> rendered when content is available — shorter, obvious, avoids DOM mutation in an event handler.
Extract a downloadBlob(name, content) helper module so the component depends on a stated operation rather than DOM mechanics.
At minimum wrap in try/finally so revokeObjectURL runs even on throw; the happy-path-only handler is TESTED-NOT-PROVED.
Did not address the DOM-dance specifically; focused on the wrong-shape RPC and the icon-not-a-button issue.
